post.caption:
Light from the first galaxies left as ordinary starlight and arrives as infrared, because space expanded the whole time it was travelling and stretched the wave along with it. To see the oldest things you have to look in a colour they were never emitted in. The catch is that everything warm glows in infrared, including the telescope, so JWST hides behind a five-layer sunshield the size of a tennis court, keeping its instruments around 40 degrees above absolute zero.
